chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasi from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far saying: 'The Qa'im has a ghaybah (occultation/disappearance), and his people deny him.' I said: 'Why is that?' He said: 'He fears.' And he pointed with his hand to his abdomen.

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The Qa'im (The Raiser/Imam), referring to the Awaited Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the occultation of the Qa'im and why did he point to his abdomen?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Zurara narrates that Imam al-Baqir (AS) foretold the Qa'im's occultation, noting that his own people would deny it due to fear of assassination or political suppression, symbolized by pointing to the abdomen. This highlights the Shia theological concept that the Imam's concealment is a divine necessity to preserve him from the plots of his enemies, a theme deeply rooted in the narrative of the Twelve Imams. The denial by 'his people' (ahluhu) often refers to the close companions or the general populace who, despite their proximity, fail to recognize the reality of the occultation amidst the prevailing political turmoil.
